name: NMI Holdings (National MI)
verdict: WATCH (lean PASS at 1.22x book near the 52wk high). CLEAN on the honesty axis — no takeaway-vs-data divergence — which is exactly why it is NOT alpha: an honestly-disclosed peak-cycle 17% ROE that has already begun to inflect (Q1-26 net incurred +4.6x). Superior of the two MIs vs MTG, but 'best fully-priced peak-harvester' is still not a buy.
entry_band: WATCH — no buy at 1.22x book near the 52wk high with the credit cycle already turning. If a starter is ever wanted: GTC BUY $34.50 (~17% below live $41.58, ~1.01x book / BVPS $33.98, ~= 52wk low $34.84), 0.5% of the $1M base (~$5k). Would NOT add above ~1.1x book. Liquidity trivially non-binding ($25.5M ADV; $5k clip <0.04% ADV). Buying a peak-cycle MI with a rising default rate + shrinking release cushion only makes sense at/around book, where you're paid for the credit risk instead of paying a premium for the benign-cycle ROE.
kill_triggers: Reserve release <~$40M/quarter-annualized (from ~$56-62M/yr) as the redundant back-book exhausts -> reported net losses roughly double and ~12% of net income / ~2pp of ROE evaporate BEFORE any HPA reversal; the 'steady 17% ROE' the screen bought re-rates to ~14%
Default rate >1.3% (now 1.17% and rising 0.81%->1.01%->1.12%->1.17%) -> the delinquency cycle turning from 'normalizing' into a genuine credit downturn
A home-price / employment reversal: MI losses are convex to HPA declines; the macro tail (shared with MTG), not underwriting (the book is FICO-757 pristine)
Persistency breaking below ~80% (now 83.4%, fading from 86.1%) if rates fall -> the second peak tailwind reverses, run-off accelerates, earned premium shrinks

court_record.dd: WATCH / lean PASS 4/10 — the highest-quality MI in the shortlist, CLEAN, but honestly-disclosed peak-cycle earnings priced at 1.22x book near the high with the reversal ALREADY in the tape. MODE B (led): (1) reported loss ratio masked ~2:1 by prior-year reserve releases — current-AY incurred (net) $78.3M/$93.2M/$114.7M (2023-25, compounding ~+22%/yr) cut by favorable release ($56.4M)/($61.7M)/($57.9M) -> reported net incurred $21.9M/$31.5M/$56.8M -> TRUE accident-year loss ratio 15.3%/16.5%/19.1% vs REPORTED 4.3%/5.6%/9.6%. (2) Honesty nuance: reserve-per-default RISING $22.9k->$25.6k = a legit release of conservative reserves as old-vintage defaults cure at high rates, NOT under-reserving or a raid — but finite. (3) Q1-2026 = the mechanism converting to earnings NOW: net incurred $20.7M vs $4.5M yoy (+4.6x) as release shrank $30.1M->$26.5M while current-year load rose $34.6M->$47.2M; default rate 1.12%->1.17%, loans-in-default 6,642->7,661->8,044, defaulted RIF +60% 2yr ($408M->$656M). (4) Persistency fading 86.1%->84.6%->83.4%, run-off 3.4%->4.5%->5.1% (elevated + reversible if rates fall = a 2nd peak tailwind). (5) Sensitivity: normalize the release to ~zero -> reported net losses ~double, ~12% of NI / ~2pp ROE gone; ex-release FY25 ROE ~14.3% not 16.2% -> 1.22x book buys a ~14% normalized ROE with no cycle discount. MODE A: CIK 1547903 confirmed; equity $2,592M / 76.29M sh -> BVPS $33.98 -> P/B 1.224 at $41.58; NO preferred (common-only), debt $425M sr notes + undrawn revolver; ROE 5yr [15.7,18.4,18.2,17.4,16.2]% (mild downtrend as equity compounds); identity implied P/E 1.224/0.162=7.6x vs reported 8.2x (EPS $5.10) — reconciles, basis clean; PMIERs available $3.50B vs required $2.06B = $1.44B excess/70% sufficiency (Q1-26 $1.47B), statutory RTC 13.0:1 vs 25:1 max; NIW WAvg FICO 757, <=679 only 3.3% of NIW = genuinely pristine underwriting (peak risk is MACRO not recklessness); buyback $450M auth 78.6M->76.3M sh, ZERO dividend (brief's '2% yield' was MTG — corrected). Takeaway-vs-data ALIGNED/CLEAN: NMIH discloses release, rising defaults, falling persistency in plain sight -> no liar to exclude -> a fundamentals call, and on fundamentals near the high it's unattractive.
court_record.adjudication: WATCH — a CLEAN, strongly-capitalized, best-in-class-quality mortgage insurer whose steady-17%-ROE is a fully-disclosed peak-cycle artifact already inflecting (Q1-26 net incurred +4.6x). Per honesty-alpha doctrine, a fully-disclosed peak is CLEAN and re-detecting disclosed bad news is not alpha -> this is a fundamental price call, and 1.22x book near the 52wk high gives none of the cushion for a cycle that has turned. NMIH is the SUPERIOR of the two shortlist MIs vs MTG (same ~1.22x P/B/~8x P/E but +13% organic book growth vs MTG +1.4%, higher/steadier ROE, FICO-757 book) — but the single MI slot only opens at a book-value entry (~$34.50), not here. No stage.

edge_explainer.market_believes: The steadiest, highest-quality mortgage insurer — a pristine FICO-757 book earning a rock-steady 17% ROE, worth a modest premium to book at ~8x earnings.
edge_explainer.we_believe: The steadiness is the TELL, not a moat. ~half the reported earnings is a FADING prior-year reserve release; strip it and it's a ~14% normalized ROE, and the credit cycle has ALREADY turned (Q1-26 net incurred +4.6x, default rate rising). At 1.22x book near the 52wk high you pay a premium for the benign-cycle ROE and get zero cushion for the turn.
edge_explainer.why_we_might_have_edge: The diligence contribution is quantifying the release-masking (true accident-year loss ratio ~19% vs reported ~10%) and showing the Q1-26 inflection — but this is a FUNDAMENTAL read, not a mispricing: the market can see all of it too.
edge_explainer.why_it_might_be_priced_in: It IS priced in the honesty sense — nothing is hidden, the identity reconciles, mgmt discloses everything. That's precisely why there's no alpha: re-detecting honestly-disclosed peak-cycle earnings isn't an edge (honesty-alpha doctrine). The name is fine; the PRICE (1.22x near the high) is the problem.
edge_explainer.what_resolves_it: The reserve release exhausting (slow) or an HPA/employment reversal (fast) normalizes the ROE down — neither is a positive catalyst. A pullback to ~book is what would make it ownable.
edge_explainer.mechanism_falsifier: If current-accident-year underwriting margins are structurally higher than pre-COVID (so 17% ROE is NOT release-flattered), 1.22x could be fair-for-a-compounder — but the true-AY loss ratio rising to 19% and the +4.6x Q1 incurred argue the release is doing the work.
edge_explainer.edge_type: VALUE (none at this price) — a clean, best-in-class but fully-priced peak-cycle insurer; ownable only at ~book (~$34.50), and even then as the compounder-of-the-two-MIs, not a table-pound. WATCH.
